fabest-hcf-competition.qualification: The archive defines a blind axial-torsion-pressure fatigue-strength exercise. It supplies load cases, geometry/protocol documents and empty submission targets, not observed target lives. It can verify input contracts and stress-state preparation but cannot independently validate a fatigue criterion, strength curve or life model.

fabest-lcf-v2.qualification: The fixed archive contains 24 calibration experiment folders, each with four numeric CSV roles and one protocol document. Archive hierarchy supplies experiment folders but no separate physical-specimen identities. The validation-target folder contains no CSV outcomes. Structure and row counts do not validate constitutive models, fatigue criteria, material transferability, blind predictions or component acceptance.

ecp-multiaxial-fatigue.qualification: Experimental life is represented once per paired FS/SWT row. Method-specific ECP factors and predicted lives remain processed outputs from the same study. Dataset files do not supply physical specimen identifiers, censoring flags, endpoint definitions, local tensor histories or finite-element meshes; none are inferred.

guided-wave-pipeline-shm.qualification: All voltage matrices are structural-health-monitoring responses from one reported laboratory tube. The final 29 acquisitions follow staged machining, not natural corrosion growth. The archive does not map files to the six machining steps or supply direct remaining thickness, timestamps or temperatures. Provider DAC remains a separate processed channel. Article text reports 2057 by 4 matrices, while every workbook sheet inspected has 2509 by 4 cells including two metadata rows; this discrepancy is retained rather than corrected.

corrosion-resistant-alloy-metrics.qualification: The CC BY 4.0 workbook is a literature compilation, not a physical-specimen database. Exact, bounded, qualitative and missing cells remain distinct. Potential references and endpoint families are not collapsed into a material score. Underlying-observation redistribution rights, specimen identity and test validity remain unresolved, and no model is fitted.

thermal-rod-transient.qualification: Primary multi-thermocouple transient runs with CC-BY-4.0 attribution. Processed h, k, boundary-ramp and power values were fitted to these same runs and are not independent experimental validation. Controller counts are not heat rate.

compiled-pipe-burst.depth_count_note: Actual primary-table values give 16 clearly above 0.8 and three within 1e-12 of 0.8; the provider description says 19 deeper defects. The tolerance here is a reporting audit, not an engineering acceptance rule.
compiled-pipe-burst.qualification: Experimental-burst/FEM-failure roles, reference tier and cell-origin audit only. Material completion, inferred widths, original specimen identity, unresolved Ma13Otros underlying references and rights, diameter/pressure convention, defect topology and test protocol require review before calibration or independent pressure validation. Raw and pointwise derived observations are excluded from redistribution; no normative bulging/flow-stress table is inferred.

crack-arrest-c1-c2.qualification: Raw signed machine channels and filename-derived temperature metadata only. No zeroing, filtering, event picking, specimen-validity decision, toughness calculation, FAD calibration or independent structural validation is performed.

The associated article resolves the conflicting workbook temperature label to degrees Celsius and identifies the dimension scale as millimetres; physical-specimen independence, row-level original literature identity and test validity remain unresolved. Article-local source groups are recorded as exact, probable-name-variant or unresolved screening links. Seven of nine article references have resolved DOIs, but no underlying-observation redistribution right is claimed. All geometry condition groups cross the provider split, so it is not treated as an independent holdout. No toughness model, standard rule or FAD boundary is fitted.

heterogeneous-wet-co2-corrosion.qualification: The source CSV has no unit labels. A separately licensed provider workbook exactly matches compilation rows 2 through 244 and qualifies those 243 rows as model-generated output, not physical observations. The remaining 184 rows still lack row-level literature sources and physical-observation independence.

he-austenite.qualification: One row is a reported condition/property, not an independently identified specimen. Preserve precharge versus in-situ exposure, weld zone and reference condition. No service suitability, fracture-growth curve or failure probability is calibrated from this compilation; raw and pointwise derived observations remain excluded.

numeric_exports.qualification: Retain original ordering, negative processed signals and uncharged controls. Clock offset disagrees with a BQ2 comment by one second. A known unquoted material-label comma is repaired only by explicit policy. The TDS hydrogen mass-ppm basis is article-supported, but detector response, source-integral unit, sample clock, physical specimen independence, boundary concentration and intrinsic lattice diffusivity remain unresolved. TDS full-range source integrals differ in scope from the room-temperature-to-260-C summary. Hashes do not establish experimental validity.

protocol_review.qualification: The article and supplement establish the TDS cylinder geometry, precharge protocol, hydrogen mass-ppm basis, nominal 100 K/h program and article-level material/exposure labels. They do not establish a measured TDS clock, curve-level physical specimen identity, initial spatial distribution, all three release boundaries or detector dynamics. Main-article TDS geometry is not the permeation membrane geometry. Declared charging current is not absorbed hydrogen flux. Permeation thickness, area, potential reference and curve-to-replicate mapping remain absent, so neither raw experiment is ready for transport inversion.

carbide-traps.qualification: Primary electrochemically charged steel trapping/desorption/permeation study with DFT, microscopy and atom-probe assets. DFT energy matrices are not measured transport histories. Reviewed CSV exports preserve signs, clocks and identities; the TDS hydrogen mass-ppm basis is now article-supported, while detector response, physical specimen mapping and transport boundary conditions remain unresolved. No project scripts, plot digitization or equilibrium/kinetic calibration are used. Raw assets and pointwise observations are excluded from public distributions.
